notes: The participle məqaddēš takes the supplied relative 'that' into its own unit, headed on the lexeme: no article morpheme stands on it, so the articleless-attributive reading (rule 41's closing paragraph, with rule 46's reasoning) governs rather than the substantival-article clause.
bi-həyôṯ is read by rule 52: the temporal preposition takes 'when' and the infinitive keeps 'shall be'.
